newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares at close to two-year high.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares at close to two-year high.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Sunday to a 23-month high in relatively low volume and one broker said investors were waiting on dividend announcements.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index rose 0.95 points to 242.6 points, the highest since early December 1994. Volume was 20.42 million pounds ($6.0 million).
"They (investors) might be waiting for balance sheets to find out how much the dividends will be," said Amr Abul-Magd, managing director of Megavest.
But Khaled Taha, deputy managing director of Triple A, told Reuters the market was still on the uptrend.
The cement and milling sectors again dominated the market and Amriyah Cement, the most active share, ended 0.50 down at 57.50. Shares worth 2.77 million pounds changed hands.
Suez Cement came second and finished at 50.00, 0.95 up, after shares worth 2.1 million pounds were traded.
North Cairo Flour Mills and Upper Egypt Flour Mills were among the market's most active shares. The Cairo miller ended at 116.25, up 2.49 pounds, but Upper Egypt finished unchanged at 51.05 pounds.
General Silos and Storage, which was privatised earlier this month, shed 0.60 to end at 41.40 pounds. The selling price on privatisation was 39 pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 361.54 points from 360.21 on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 171.52 from 170.82.
